title: Psalms Chapter 58 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 58 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 58 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 58.

questions.question: Who is the psalmist addressing in Psalms 58:1?
questions.correctAnswer: O congregation
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:1 specifically addresses 'O congregation' asking if they speak righteousness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 58:2, what do the people work in their hearts?
questions.correctAnswer: Wickedness
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:2 states that in heart they work wickedness.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 58:3 says that the wicked start speaking lies only when they grow old.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:3 says the wicked go astray as soon as they are born, speaking lies, not only when they grow old.

questions.question: What animal is used as a comparison to describe the poison of the wicked in Psalms 58:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Serpent
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:4 compares their poison to the poison of a serpent.

questions.question: In Psalms 58:1, what two qualities are questioned about the congregation?
questions.correctAnswer: Speaking righteousness and judging uprightly
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:1 asks if they indeed speak righteousness and judge uprightly.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 58:2, the violence of their hands is weighed in the earth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:2 states they weigh the violence of their hands in the earth.

questions.question: How does Psalms 58:3 describe the wicked from birth?
options: Estranged from the womb and speaking lies
questions.correctAnswer: Estranged from the womb and speaking lies
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:3 says the wicked are estranged from the womb and speak lies as soon as they are born.

questions.question: Which characteristic is given to the wicked in Psalms 58:4 besides having poison like a serpent?
options: They are like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear
questions.correctAnswer: They are like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:4 describes them as like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 58:1 includes the term 'Michtam of David' as part of its title.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The heading in Psalms 58:1 includes the phrase 'Michtam of David.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 58:2, what do the wicked weigh in the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: The violence of their hands
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:2 says they weigh the violence of their hands in the earth.

questions.question: In Psalms 58:3, from what are the wicked estranged?
questions.correctAnswer: The womb
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:3 states the wicked are estranged from the womb.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 58:4 says the wicked are like the deaf adder that listens carefully to charmers.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:4 says the wicked are like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear, so they do not listen.

questions.question: Which comes first in Psalms 58:1-4: the question about judging uprightly or the description of the wicked as estranged from the womb?
options: Description of the wicked as estranged from the womb
Description of poison like a serpent
questions.correctAnswer: Question about judging uprightly
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:1 first asks about judging uprightly before describing the wicked in verse 3.

questions.question: What is the attitude of the wicked according to Psalms 58:2?
options: They work wickedness in their heart
questions.correctAnswer: They work wickedness in their heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:2 clearly states that in their heart they work wickedness.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the wicked's behavior from birth in Psalms 58:3?
options: They go astray and speak lies
questions.correctAnswer: They go astray and speak lies
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:3 says the wicked go astray as soon as born, speaking lies.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 58 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 58 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 58:5, how do the wicked respond to the voice of charmers?
options: They ignore it and do not hearken
They seek to learn from them
questions.correctAnswer: They ignore it and do not hearken
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:5 states that the wicked will not hearken to the voice of charmers, indicating their stubborn refusal to listen.

questions.question: What is the plea made to God in Psalms 58:6 regarding the wicked?
options: Remove them peacefully from the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Break their teeth and power
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:6 specifically asks God to break the teeth of the wicked, symbolizing a request to remove their power to harm.

questions.question: How does Psalms 58:7 describe the fate of the wicked when God acts against them?
options: They will be honored by men
They will melt away like running waters
They will be hidden in the mountains
They will grow strong like lions
questions.correctAnswer: They will melt away like running waters
questions.explanation: The verse uses the imagery of waters that run continually to illustrate the complete and unstoppable disappearance of the wicked.

questions.question: What simile does Psalms 58:8 use to describe how the wicked will pass away?
questions.correctAnswer: Like a snail which melteth
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:8 compares the fate of the wicked to a melting snail, emphasizing their gradual and inevitable demise.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the stubbornness described in Psalms 58:5 and the plea in Psalms 58:6?
options: Because they listen, the psalmist asks God to bless them
Because they refuse to listen, the psalmist asks God to break their power
Because they charm others, the psalmist asks God to protect them
Because they repent, the psalmist asks God to forgive them
questions.correctAnswer: Because they refuse to listen, the psalmist asks God to break their power
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:5 shows the wicked's refusal to listen, which leads to the plea in 58:6 for God to break their teeth, symbolizing their removal of power.

questions.question: What lesson about divine justice can we learn from the imagery of melting waters and a melting snail in Psalms 58:7-8?
options: The wicked will gradually disappear under God's judgment
The wicked will be unstoppable forces
The wicked will be transformed into righteous people
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked will gradually disappear under God's judgment
questions.explanation: The passage uses natural melting imagery to illustrate the gradual and certain destruction of the wicked by God's judgment (Psalms 58:7-8).

questions.question: How does Psalms 58:9 describe God's swift action against the wicked?
options: Taking them away like a gentle breeze
Removing them like a whirlwind before the thorns are felt
questions.correctAnswer: Removing them like a whirlwind before the thorns are felt
questions.explanation: The verse portrays God removing the wicked swiftly and powerfully, like a whirlwind, even before the pain of thorns is felt.

questions.question: According to Psalms 58:10, what will the righteous do when they see God's vengeance?
options: Rejoice and wash their feet in the blood of the wicked
Pray for mercy on the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Rejoice and wash their feet in the blood of the wicked
questions.explanation: The verse states that the righteous will rejoice and symbolically wash their feet in the blood of the wicked, celebrating God's justice.

questions.question: What assurance does Psalms 58:11 give about God's judgment on earth?
options: God does not judge on earth
There is no reward for righteousness
God is a righteous judge who rewards the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God is a righteous judge who rewards the righteous
questions.explanation: The verse affirms that God judges righteously on earth and rewards those who are righteous.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 58:3 teaches that wickedness begins from birth and is characterized by speaking lies.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:3 clearly states that the wicked are estranged from the womb and speak lies from birth.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 58:4, the wicked are compared to a serpent that listens carefully to warnings.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:4 compares the wicked to a deaf adder that stops its ear, refusing to listen, not one that listens carefully.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist asks God in Psalms 58:6 to empower the wicked like young lions.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In Psalms 58:6, the psalmist actually asks God to break the great teeth of the young lions, symbolizing a desire to weaken the wicked.

questions.question: How does Psalms 58:1 challenge the congregation regarding their judgment?
options: It questions whether they truly judge uprightly
It commands them to judge harshly
questions.correctAnswer: It questions whether they truly judge uprightly
questions.explanation: The verse asks if the congregation speaks righteousness and judges uprightly, challenging their integrity in judgment.

questions.question: According to Psalms 58:2, what do the wicked do in their hearts despite outward appearances?
questions.correctAnswer: Work wickedness and weigh violence
questions.explanation: The verse reveals that in their hearts, the wicked work wickedness and plot violence, regardless of their outward actions.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 58:7-8, what does the psalmist imply about the certainty of God's judgment on the wicked?
options: It may or may not happen
It is slow but sure like melting waters and snails
It will happen only if the wicked repent
It is symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: It is slow but sure like melting waters and snails
questions.explanation: The imagery of melting waters and snails indicates a gradual yet unstoppable process of judgment on the wicked.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 58 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 58.

questions.question: According to Psalms 58:9, how does God take away the wicked before their pots can feel the thorns?
questions.correctAnswer: As with a whirlwind
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:9 states that God takes them away 'as with a whirlwind, both living, and in his wrath,' emphasizing swift and powerful divine judgment.

questions.question: What does the righteous do when he sees the vengeance of God according to Psalms 58:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Rejoice
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:10 says 'The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance,' showing that the righteous take joy in God’s just judgment against the wicked.

questions.question: In Psalms 58:10, what symbolic act is mentioned that the righteous perform related to the blood of the wicked?
options: Wash his feet in the blood of the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Wash his feet in the blood of the wicked
questions.explanation: The verse uses vivid imagery, stating the righteous shall 'wash his feet in the blood of the wicked,' symbolizing triumph and justice.

questions.question: What affirmation is made about God in Psalms 58:11?
options: He is a God that judgeth in the earth
He is a God of mercy only
He is silent in the face of injustice
questions.correctAnswer: He is a God that judgeth in the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:11 declares God’s role as the righteous judge on earth, affirming divine justice.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s justice as seen in Psalms 58:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 32:4
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:4 similarly affirms God as a just and faithful judge, paralleling Psalms 58:11’s theme of divine justice.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Psalms 58:8 with the phrases 'like a snail which melteth' and 'like the untimely birth of a woman'?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:8 uses similes to compare the fate of the wicked to fragile and sorrowful phenomena, emphasizing their swift demise.

questions.question: What Hebrew word underlies the term 'vengeance' in Psalms 58:10, and what is its significance?
questions.correctAnswer: Nakam, meaning divine retribution
questions.explanation: 'Nakam' is the Hebrew word for vengeance, emphasizing God’s role in executing righteous retribution as seen in Psalms 58:10.

questions.question: According to Psalms 58:7, what is the fate of the wicked when God bends his bow to shoot his arrows?
options: They shall be cut in pieces
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be cut in pieces
questions.explanation: The verse uses vivid imagery to describe the destruction of the wicked under divine judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 58:3 states that the wicked are estranged from the womb and go astray as soon as they are born.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:3 clearly states that 'The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born,' indicating inherent wickedness.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 58:5 says the deaf adder hearkens to the voice of charmers and is easily charmed.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:5 states that the deaf adder 'will not hearken to the voice of charmers, charming never so wisely,' indicating stubbornness and resistance.

questions.question: How does Psalms 58:6 metaphorically describe the wicked, calling for God to break their teeth?
questions.correctAnswer: Young lions
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:6 petitions God to 'break out the great teeth of the young lions,' symbolizing the dangerous power of the wicked that needs to be neutralized.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s judgment and the fate of the wicked as presented in Psalms 58?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 12:19
questions.explanation: Romans 12:19 emphasizes leaving vengeance to God, paralleling Psalms 58’s theme of divine judgment upon the wicked.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'pots' and 'thorns' imagery in Psalms 58:9 in the ancient Near Eastern cultural context?
options: It symbolizes domestic life and sudden danger
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes domestic life and sudden danger
questions.explanation: In ancient Near Eastern culture, pots were common household items, and thorns could injure them suddenly, symbolizing the swift and unexpected judgment described in Psalms 58:9.

questions.question: What theme from Psalms 58 is fulfilled in the prophetic judgment described in Isaiah 59:15-16?
options: God’s wrath and justice intervening against wickedness
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wrath and justice intervening against wickedness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 59:15-16 describes God’s justice and wrath against iniquity, echoing the themes of divine vengeance and righteousness in Psalms 58.

questions.question: What does the term 'Michtam' in the title of Psalms 58 likely indicate about its content or style?
questions.correctAnswer: A golden or precious poem
questions.explanation: 'Michtam' is often understood as a term denoting a golden or precious poem, indicating the psalm’s special value or style, relevant to Psalms 58:1.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 58 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 58 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human nature is illustrated by the statement, "The wicked are estranged from the womb" in Psalms 58:3?
options: Original sin and innate human depravity
The neutrality of human nature at birth
questions.correctAnswer: Original sin and innate human depravity
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:3 states that the wicked are estranged from the womb and go astray from birth, indicating a doctrine of original sin and inherent human depravity, consistent with Romans 5:12 where sin entered through one man affecting all humanity.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is primarily demonstrated by the petition, "Break their teeth, O God..." in Psalms 58:6?
options: God’s justice and power to punish
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice and power to punish
questions.explanation: In Psalms 58:6, the plea to break the teeth of the wicked reflects God’s attribute of executing righteous justice and exercising power to punish evildoers, paralleling Romans 12:19 about God’s vengeance.

questions.question: How does Psalms 58:1 reflect on human responsibility in judgment?
options: It questions whether humans truly judge righteously
It states humans always judge correctly
questions.correctAnswer: It questions whether humans truly judge righteously
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:1 asks if the congregation and sons of men judge uprightly, revealing the human responsibility to judge rightly but also a skepticism about their actual righteousness, consistent with Ecclesiastes 7:20 about no one being perfectly righteous.

questions.question: What theological insight about divine retribution is conveyed by combining Psalms 58:7 and Psalms 58:9?
options: The wicked will be swiftly and completely destroyed by God’s wrath
The wicked will repent before punishment
The wicked will be forgiven after a trial period
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked will be swiftly and completely destroyed by God’s wrath
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 9 together describe the wicked melting away like water or a snail and being taken away by a whirlwind in God’s wrath, teaching the doctrine of swift and total divine judgment, consistent with Nahum 1:3.

questions.question: According to Psalms 58:4, what metaphor is used to describe the nature of the wicked, and what does it imply about their character?
options: They are like a serpent’s poison, implying deadly deceit and hardness of heart
They are like a peaceful dove, implying innocence
They are like a flowing river, implying purity
They are like a burning fire, implying zeal for God
questions.correctAnswer: They are like a serpent’s poison, implying deadly deceit and hardness of heart
questions.explanation: Verse 4 compares the wicked’s poison to that of a serpent and a deaf adder, indicating their dangerous, deceitful, and unresponsive nature, paralleling Romans 3:13 about corrupt speech and hearts.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching on divine judgment and reward is taught by Psalms 58:10 and Psalms 58:11?
options: The righteous will rejoice and receive a reward because God judges the earth
The wicked will be rewarded for their deeds
God does not judge the earth
All receive the same fate regardless of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous will rejoice and receive a reward because God judges the earth
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 11 affirm that the righteous will rejoice upon seeing God’s vengeance and that God rewards the righteous as the judge of the earth, illustrating the doctrine of final judgment and divine recompense, supported by 2 Corinthians 5:10.

questions.question: In Psalms 58:2, what is revealed about the internal disposition of the wicked despite outward appearance?
options: They work wickedness in their hearts despite any outward appearance
They are outwardly wicked but inwardly righteous
They are neutral in heart but act wickedly
Their hearts are pure though their hands do violence
questions.correctAnswer: They work wickedness in their hearts despite any outward appearance
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states that in their hearts they work wickedness and weigh violence, indicating the internal sinfulness that drives external evil, consistent with Jeremiah 17:9 about the deceitful heart.

questions.question: What does Psalms 58:5 teach about the stubbornness of the wicked in relation to divine warnings or wisdom?
options: They refuse to listen even to the wisest charmers or warnings
They eagerly accept correction and wisdom
They are easily persuaded by charmers
They repent quickly upon hearing warnings
questions.correctAnswer: They refuse to listen even to the wisest charmers or warnings
questions.explanation: Verse 5 describes the wicked as refusing to hearken to charmers’ voices, symbolizing their hardened resistance to correction and wisdom, paralleling Proverbs 1:24 on rejecting wisdom’s call.

questions.question: How does Psalms 58:8 use imagery to convey the sudden and premature destruction of the wicked, and what theological principle does this support?
options: They perish like an untimely birth, supporting the principle of sudden divine judgment
They grow slowly like a tree, supporting patience
They shine like stars, supporting eternal life
They are protected like a lion’s den, supporting security
questions.correctAnswer: They perish like an untimely birth, supporting the principle of sudden divine judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 8 compares the wicked’s demise to an untimely birth that never sees the sun, teaching the doctrine that divine judgment can come suddenly and unexpectedly, consistent with 1 Thessalonians 5:3.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by the statement in Psalms 58:11 that He is "a God that judgeth in the earth"?
options: God’s role as the righteous and sovereign judge over all creation
God’s role as a distant and uninvolved deity
God’s role as only a creator with no judgment
God’s role as a passive observer
questions.correctAnswer: God’s role as the righteous and sovereign judge over all creation
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:11 emphasizes God’s attribute as the righteous judge who exercises sovereign judgment on earth, affirming His justice and authority, in agreement with Psalm 9:8.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s judgment described in Psalms 58 is arbitrary and cruel. What does Psalms 58:10-11 actually teach about the nature of divine judgment?
options: Divine judgment is just, rewarding the righteous and punishing the wicked
Divine judgment is random and unjust
God shows favoritism to the wicked
Judgment is delayed indefinitely without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment is just, rewarding the righteous and punishing the wicked
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 show that the righteous rejoice in God’s just vengeance and that God rewards righteousness, demonstrating that divine judgment is fair and purposeful, consistent with Romans 2:6.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about human wickedness and divine power is taught when considering Psalms 58:3-4 alongside Psalms 58:6-7?
options: Human wickedness is innate and harmful, but God has the power to decisively destroy it
Human wickedness is temporary and self-correcting
God is powerless against human wickedness
Human wickedness is harmless and unnoticed by God
questions.correctAnswer: Human wickedness is innate and harmful, but God has the power to decisively destroy it
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 describe innate wickedness like serpent poison, while 6-7 invoke God breaking the teeth and cutting the wicked like water, teaching that God’s power overcomes innate sinfulness, in line with Colossians 2:15.

questions.question: How does Psalms 58:9 contribute to the biblical narrative of God’s wrath against sin?
options: It portrays God’s wrath as active and decisive in removing the wicked swiftly
It suggests God is indifferent to sin
It implies God’s wrath is slow and hesitant
It denies any divine punishment for sin
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays God’s wrath as active and decisive in removing the wicked swiftly
questions.explanation: Verse 9 describes God taking away the wicked with a whirlwind in His wrath, illustrating the biblical theme of God’s active and just wrath against sin, as echoed in Nahum 1:2.

questions.question: What does Psalms 58:1-2 combined teach about the contrast between human justice and divine justice?
options: Human justice is often corrupted by wicked hearts, unlike divine justice which is righteous
Human justice is always perfect and mirrors divine justice
Human justice is unrelated to divine justice
Human justice is superior to divine justice
questions.correctAnswer: Human justice is often corrupted by wicked hearts, unlike divine justice which is righteous
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 question the righteousness of human judgment and reveal wickedness in the heart, implying human justice is flawed, contrasting with God’s perfect justice as shown later in the chapter, consistent with Isaiah 1:17.

questions.question: How do Psalms 58:8 and Psalms 58:10 together inform the doctrine of eschatological vindication for the righteous?
options: The wicked perish prematurely while the righteous rejoice in God’s final vindication
Both the wicked and righteous perish without hope
The righteous face premature death while the wicked rejoice
There is no final vindication for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked perish prematurely while the righteous rejoice in God’s final vindication
questions.explanation: Verse 8 describes the premature destruction of the wicked, and verse 10 shows the righteous rejoicing at God’s vengeance, together teaching the doctrine of eschatological vindication where God ultimately rewards righteousness, as echoed in Revelation 20:12-13.
